_readme: Hand-edited. One entry per project: id -> where it comes from. Read by prefill/assemble.mjs; see data/README.md for the fields. Only entries with confirmed:"mod" show on the site; confirmed:"suggested" entries wait for a mod.

librewolf.why: A fork of Firefox with privacy and security settings changed; its releases carry Firefox's version numbers.
librewolf.differs: Firefox with tracking blocked and stricter privacy settings by default
librewolf.differsFromChild: LibreWolf: Firefox with tracking blocked by default

zen-browser.why: A fork of Firefox introduced in 2024, focused on privacy, customizability and design.
zen-browser.differs: Firefox with a customizable, calmer layout and add-on themes called Mods
zen-browser.differsFromChild: Zen: Firefox with a calmer, customizable layout

tor-browser.why: A modified Firefox ESR (Firefox's long-support version) bundled with the Tor network software.
tor-browser.differs: Firefox that hides your location by routing traffic through Tor
tor-browser.differsFromChild: Tor Browser: Firefox that hides your location through Tor

floorp.why: A Japanese browser based on Firefox, focused on customizing the interface.
floorp.differs: Firefox with workspaces, split view and many ways to customize the look
floorp.differsFromChild: Floorp: Firefox with workspaces and split view

mullvad-browser.why: Made by Mullvad VPN together with the Tor Project, which describe it as "a Tor Browser to use without the Tor Network".
mullvad-browser.differs: Tor Browser's privacy protections without the Tor network, for use with a VPN
mullvad-browser.differsFromChild: Mullvad Browser: Tor Browser without Tor

ungoogled-chromium.why: Chromium with its dependence on Google web services removed.
ungoogled-chromium.differs: Chromium with Google's web services and tracking removed
ungoogled-chromium.differsFromChild: Ungoogled Chromium: Chromium without Google services

brave.why: A browser based on the Chromium web browser, made by Brave Software.
brave.differs: Chromium-based, with a built-in ad blocker and crypto rewards
brave.differsFromChild: Brave: Chromium with a built-in ad blocker

forgejo.why: Started in December 2022 as a fork of Gitea, after Gitea's trademarks and operations were moved to a for-profit company.
forgejo.differs: Gitea's community-run fork, governed by a non-profit
forgejo.differsFromChild: Forgejo: community-run fork governed by a non-profit

gitea.why: Started in November 2016 as a fork of Gogs, to develop it as a community-run project.
gitea.differs: Gogs forked to be developed by its community, and grown into a fuller platform

nextcloud.why: Started in 2016 as a fork of ownCloud by Frank Karlitschek, ownCloud's founder and then CTO, after he left the company.
nextcloud.differs: ownCloud's fork, started by its founder after he left the company
nextcloud.differsFromChild: Nextcloud: fork started by ownCloud's founder

comaps.why: A community-led fork of Organic Maps, which itself began as a fork of Maps.me.
comaps.differs: Organic Maps run by its community instead of a single company

heliboard.why: Describes itself as "based on AOSP / OpenBoard".
heliboard.differs: OpenBoard with more customization, kept up to date

kilo-code.why: Launched in March 2025 as a fork of Roo Code, which was itself derived from Cline.
kilo-code.differs: AI coding agent descended from Roo Code and Cline, with its own platform
kilo-code.differsFromChild: Kilo Code: fork of Roo Code, itself from Cline

vaultwarden.why: An unofficial rewrite of the Bitwarden server that works with Bitwarden's apps; it was called Bitwarden_RS until renamed to avoid confusion with the official server.
vaultwarden.label: Works with Bitwarden's apps
vaultwarden.differs: Lightweight server that works with Bitwarden's apps
vaultwarden.differsFromChild: Vaultwarden: lightweight unofficial server for Bitwarden apps

mbin.why: A fork and continuation of kbin.
mbin.differs: Carries on kbin, which is no longer maintained

vane-formerly-perplexica.why: Perplexica was renamed Vane; Perplexica's old GitHub address now forwards to Vane's.

keepassxc.why: A community fork of KeePassX; KeePassX announced on 2021-12-09 that it is no longer developed.

fossify-calendar.why: Fossify emerged as a fork of the discontinued Simple Mobile Tools apps, to continue them.
fossify-calendar.differs: Continues Simple Calendar after the original was discontinued

fossify-gallery.why: Fossify emerged as a fork of the discontinued Simple Mobile Tools apps, to continue them.
fossify-gallery.differs: Continues Simple Gallery after the original was discontinued

simple-keyboard.why: A separate app by a different developer; it is not a fork of the Simple Mobile Tools keyboard of the same name.
simple-keyboard.differs: Not related to the Simple Mobile Tools keyboard of the same name

bazzite.why: Built from Fedora's Atomic Desktops (Kinoite and Silverblue) through the Universal Blue project.
bazzite.differs: Fedora Atomic with gaming-focused setup built in
bazzite.differsFromChild: Bazzite: Fedora Atomic set up for gaming

linux-mint.why: Based on Ubuntu and uses its package repositories.
linux-mint.differs: Ubuntu with a more Windows-like desktop
linux-mint.differsFromChild: Linux Mint: Ubuntu with a Windows-like desktop

pop-os.why: Based on Ubuntu; developed by System76.
pop-os.differs: Ubuntu with System76's own setup and COSMIC desktop

ubuntu.why: A Linux distribution based on Debian.
ubuntu.differs: Debian with scheduled releases and company backing from Canonical

cachyos.why: A Linux distribution based on Arch Linux.
cachyos.differs: Arch Linux with performance-tuned packages and a friendlier installer

postmarketos.why: postmarketOS was renamed Nura; postmarketos.org now forwards to nura.eco, which says Nura was formerly known as postmarketOS.

mlcraft.why: MLCraft was renamed Synmetrix; the project's README says "Synmetrix (prev. MLCraft)".

libreoffice-writer.why: Created in 2010 as a fork of OpenOffice.org; Apache OpenOffice is the other continuation of that code.
libreoffice-writer.differs: Fork of OpenOffice.org, a separate continuation from Apache OpenOffice

libreoffice-calc.why: Created in 2010 as a fork of OpenOffice.org; Apache OpenOffice is the other continuation of that code.
libreoffice-calc.differs: Fork of OpenOffice.org, a separate continuation from Apache OpenOffice

libreoffice-impress.why: Created in 2010 as a fork of OpenOffice.org; Apache OpenOffice is the other continuation of that code.
libreoffice-impress.differs: Fork of OpenOffice.org, a separate continuation from Apache OpenOffice

collabora-online.why: An online office suite made by Collabora and based on LibreOffice's code.
collabora-online.label: Built on LibreOffice
collabora-online.differs: LibreOffice that runs in a web browser, for editing together
collabora-online.differsFromChild: Collabora Online: LibreOffice in the browser

valkey.why: Forked in 2024 from the last BSD-licensed Redis (7.2.4) by Linux Foundation members, after Redis moved to a source-available license.
valkey.differs: Redis's fork from the last open-license version, run by the Linux Foundation
valkey.differsFromChild: Valkey: fork from Redis's last open license

opentofu.why: Started in 2023 as a fork of Terraform under the MPL, after HashiCorp relicensed Terraform under the Business Source License.
opentofu.differs: Terraform's fork under an open license, run by the Linux Foundation

vscodium.why: Build scripts that turn Microsoft's open-source vscode code into freely licensed downloads without Microsoft's branding and telemetry; the project says it is not a fork.
vscodium.label: Open-source build of Visual Studio Code
vscodium.differs: VS Code built without Microsoft's branding and telemetry

lineageos.why: A community fork and successor to CyanogenMod, launched in December 2016.
lineageos.differs: Successor to CyanogenMod, which shut down

e-os.why: A fork of LineageOS (formerly called Eelo) that adds its own online services.
e-os.differs: LineageOS with Google services removed and its own online services
e-os.differsFromChild: /e/OS: LineageOS without Google, plus its own cloud

element.why: Renamed from Riot to Element in July 2020.

openclaw.why: Renamed twice in January 2026, first to Moltbot and three days later to OpenClaw.

kodi.why: Renamed from XBMC to Kodi in July 2014.

jellyfin.why: Started in December 2018 as a fork of Emby.
jellyfin.differs: Emby's fork, started in 2018 as a community project

quillpad.why: A fork of Quillnote, started so development could continue.
quillpad.differs: Continues Quillnote so development can go on

friction.why: Says it is based on enve, an earlier 2D animation program.
friction.differs: Animation program based on enve's earlier code

trilium-notes.why: The original developer, zadam, gave the Trilium repository to the TriliumNext community project.
trilium-notes.differs: Trilium continued by the TriliumNext community after its creator handed it over

gitlab-community-edition.why: GitLab's free, open-source edition; GitLab also sells a paid Enterprise Edition.
gitlab-community-edition.differs: GitLab's free open-source edition; the paid Enterprise Edition adds more
